disclaimer: NU Map is an independent, student-built planner. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or officially connected to Northeastern University. Data is scraped from Northeastern's public catalog and refreshed on a schedule; always confirm with the official catalog and an academic advisor.

legend.prereqs: Flat token list: course refs {subject, number, minGrade} joined by 'And'/'Or' strings; nested arrays are parenthesized groups. minGrade is the minimum passing grade required.
legend.coreqs: Courses that must be taken in the same term.
legend.offerings.terms: Past/scheduled terms by Banner code (YYYY = academic-year END year; Fall runs in YYYY-1). sections/enrolled/capacity are snapshots from the scheduled scrape, NOT live seat availability.
legend.offerings.typicalDays: Weekdays on which at least 50% of recent sections met.
legend.offerings.daysPct: Percent of recent sections meeting on each weekday (M/T/W/Th/F).
legend.offerings.meetingPatterns: [pattern, percent-of-sections] pairs; in patterns like 'MWR', R means Thursday.
legend.instructors: Per season. sharePct = average percent of that season's enrolled students taught by this professor (recent terms). 'reviews' links their RateMyHusky page when one exists.
legend.level: undergrad for course numbers below 5000, grad otherwise.
legend.typicallyOffered: Seasons in which the course was scheduled in at least two-thirds of that season's terms on record since it first appeared — a pattern, not a guarantee.
legend.unlocks: Courses that list this course in their prerequisites — what taking it opens up.
legend.nuPath: NUpath general-education attributes this course carries.
legend.repeatable: Whether the course may be taken more than once for credit (repeatMax / repeatMaxSH cap it).

courses.subject: FRNH
courses.title: Elementary French 1
courses.description: Designed for students with very little or no prior knowledge of French. Provides a lively introduction to basic oral expression, listening comprehension, and elementary reading and writing. Each lesson incorporates helpful information about daily life in France and the varied cultures within the world of French speakers. Laboratory practice complements class work, enables students to work aloud at their own speed, reinforces their acquisition of essential structures, and acquaints them with a vast library of audio-visual resources.

courses.subject: FRNH
courses.title: Elementary French 2
courses.description: Continues FRNH 1101. Reviews and continues the study of grammar and basic language skills. Offers progressively more intensive practice in oral and written communication. Laboratory practice complements class work, enables students to work aloud at their own speed, reinforces their acquisition of essential structures, and acquaints them with a vast library of audio-visual resources.

courses.subject: FRNH
courses.title: French Film and Culture
courses.description: Provides an introduction to some of the qualities that have made French film one of the great national cinemas. Focuses on both form and content; relates outstanding directors’ major works to the French culture and society of their period. Conducted in English.

courses.subject: FRNH
courses.title: Introduction to French Culture
courses.description: Explores contemporary France and French mentality through lectures, screenings, readings, and discussions. Topics covered include the modern vs. the traditional family, social reproduction, gender norms, culture and social distinction, the concept of “grandeur,” identity, and immigration. Offers students an opportunity to evaluate historical and sociological readings, films, documentaries, and TV commercials; to compare French and American systems; and to consider contemporary human and social behaviors in the face of globalization. Conducted in English.

courses.subject: FRNH
courses.title: Special Topics in Francophone Culture
courses.description: Explores in-depth a specific topic related to Francophone culture, literature, and/or language. Taught in English. May be repeated twice.

courses.subject: FRNH
courses.title: Elective
courses.description: Offers elective credit for courses taken at other academic institutions. May be repeated without limit.

courses.subject: FRNH
courses.title: Intermediate French 1
courses.description: Emphasizes further vocabulary building and mastery of fine points of grammar through written composition, prepared oral reports, and reading and discussion from current French periodicals.

courses.subject: FRNH
courses.title: Intermediate French 2
courses.description: Continues FRNH 2101. Stresses the fundamentals of French to promote effective self-expression through speaking and writing and to explore the idiomatic aspects of the language. Through progressive class discussions and oral and written commentaries, students analyze a contemporary French novel or a French cultural reader, screenplay, or collection of short stories. Strives to help students read and comprehend modern French writing with confidence, and to be able to talk and write about it in good French. Provides preparation for advanced courses.

courses.subject: FRNH
courses.title: Specialized Instruction in French
courses.description: Focuses on developing students’ language proficiency and cultural competence within a specific context. May be repeated twice for a maximum of 12 semester hours with department approval.

courses.subject: FRNH
courses.title: Elective
courses.description: Offers elective credit for courses taken at other academic institutions. May be repeated without limit.

courses.subject: FRNH
courses.title: Advanced French 1
courses.description: Continues further development of vocabulary. Offers students an opportunity to continue to master grammar and conversation through advanced reading, composition, grammar review, and listening skills. Whenever possible, offers students an opportunity to engage in local community activities to enhance communication skills and cultural knowledge.

prereqs.note: French Placement Test with a score of 411

courses.subject: FRNH
courses.title: Advanced French 2
courses.description: Builds on FRNH 3101 and continues further development of vocabulary. Offers students an opportunity to continue to master grammar and conversation through advanced reading, composition, grammar review, and listening skills. Whenever possible, offers students an opportunity to engage in local community activities to enhance communication skills and cultural knowledge.

courses.subject: FRNH
courses.title: The Structure of French
courses.description: Introduces the basic principles of linguistic analysis by examining the structure of modern French. Emphasizes descriptive (and not prescriptive) analysis of the phonetic, phonological, morphological, syntactic, and semantic characteristics of modern French in its everyday use.

courses.subject: FRNH
courses.title: Special Topics in French
courses.description: Focuses on specific aspects of French language and culture. May be repeated up to twice for a maximum of 12 semester hours, when topics vary.

courses.subject: FRNH
courses.title: French Pop Culture
courses.description: Focuses on contemporary French society and pop culture. Fosters a nuanced understanding of modern French cultural dynamics and perspectives through an in-depth exploration of diverse sources. Examines a wide range of topics including media, cinema, music, art, fashion, and social issues. Aims to enhance students' proficiency in French by emphasizing contextual and critical analysis, while providing a platform for developing their intercultural awareness. Conducted entirely in French.

courses.subject: FRNH
courses.title: Cultural Engagement: Dialogue of Civilizations
courses.description: Engages students on-site with the culture(s) and the communities of French-speaking regions. Emphasizes the complexity, transnationalism, and interdisciplinary nature of culture(s). Employs a range of methodological approaches to describe and analyze how cultural practices, objects, texts, and meanings are created, distributed, and exchanged within particular social groups or geographic areas. Explores questions of cultural identity, meaning, representation, policy formations, and ideologies. In addition to regular in-class lectures and activities, offers students an opportunity to engage in dialogue with members of the local communities about their perspectives on relevant cultural topics and everyday experiences. May be repeated once. Conducted in French.

courses.title: Directed Study
courses.description: Offers students a way of going beyond work given in the regular curriculum; may also enable students to complete major or minor requirements in certain situations. Priority is given to language majors and to juniors and seniors. May be repeated without limit.

courses.subject: FRNH
courses.title: Directed Study
courses.description: Offers independent work under the direction of members of the department on a chosen topic. Course content depends on instructor. May be repeated without limit.
